blocks.html:
The Deploy App is a handful of small services. Each one is owned separately, but they all depend on two shared things: a common identity layer and a private CA. This page is the map of what's running, how it gets deployed, and where to look first when something breaks.

High-level picture

The platform ships as Zarf packages built in CI, both online and offline install bundles. The platform itself holds only platform-level features: the identity layer (Keycloak plus OpenLDAP), Rasenmaeher, the shared CA, the core operators, and monitoring. Every integrated product is owned in its own repository and produces its own Zarf package. How a given repo builds that package, whether through Kustomize or something else, is up to that repo. At the platform boundary, the only thing that matters is that the same Zarf packages come out of CI and deploy together. So treat the repo-specific details below as the current transition-phase layout. They are not fixed contracts.

flowchart TB
traefik["Traefik ingress - HTTP and TCP passthrough"]
rm["Rasenmaeher UI and API - rmui, rmapi"]
idp["Identity - Keycloak and OpenLDAP"]
apps["Integrated apps - TAK, Battlelog, MediaMTX, ..."]
infra["Shared infra - CFSSL CA, cert-manager, external-secrets, CloudNativePG, trust-manager"]
traefik --> rm
traefik --> idp
traefik --> apps
idp --> rm
idp -->|LDAP / OIDC| apps
rm --> infra
idp --> infra
apps --> infra

Onboarding runs through rmapi and rmui. The bootstrap itself is miniwerk, a one-shot job that sets up the Keycloak realms and registers whatever products are listed in MW_PRODUCTS. After that, every integrated app talks back to rmapi and authenticates its users through Keycloak. Service-to-service trust is handled by the cluster's own CFSSL CA, with trust-manager pushing those certificates around.

Components by folder

Each entry below maps to a k8s/<folder>/ directory. Keep in mind this layout is a snapshot of where things sit while everything still lives in one repo. The modules are the stable part. The exact folder paths and the tooling around them are not promises. The platform modules (identity, Rasenmaeher, the CA, the core operators, monitoring) stay in the platform package. The integrated products are slowly moving out into their own repos, each with its own Zarf package.

Cluster infrastructure (operators and ingress)

Folder Role
cloudnative-pg PostgreSQL operator. Owns the rmapi, keycloak, and battlelog databases.
keycloak-operator CRDs and controller for Keycloak.
external-secrets-operator Pulls secrets from external stores into the cluster.
cert-manager, cert-manager-clusterissuers Certificate issuance and cluster-wide issuers.
trust-manager Distributes CA bundles into namespaces that need them.
traefik Ingress and TCP passthrough for TAK and mTLS.
prometheus-operator, grafana-operator Monitoring CRDs.
metrics-server HPA and kubectl top source (cloud overlay).
longhorn Storage option (commented out in main/local).
projectcontour Alternative ingress (not in the active phase composition).

Platform core

Folder Role
opendefense-cfssl The internal Certificate Authority.
opendefense-pki PKI glue and CA bundle resources used by other services.
opendefense-system Keycloak, OpenLDAP, miniwerk, rmapi, and rmui in one namespace (opendefense-system).

Integrated applications

Folder Role
battlelog Live event log (Liveloki). Lives in namespace app-battlelog.
tak ATAK / TAK server. CoT TCP streaming and mTLS subdomain.
mtx MediaMTX streaming server (RTMPS, RTSPS, SRT, HLS, WebRTC).
monitoring/{alloy,grafana,loki,prometheus} Observability stack composed under main/<env>/monitoring/.

Legacy and reference

k8s/pvarki-keycloak/ is an aggregate left over from earlier work. Don't use it as a template for new services. It crams a lot of unrelated concerns into one base, which is exactly what we're trying to move away from. agents.md explains the reasoning in more detail.

Deploy phases

The cluster comes up in four ordered slices. Each one has to roll out fully before the next is applied, and task deploy:_apply is what enforces that.

  1. infra-phase1, operators and ingress. CloudNativePG, Keycloak operator, External Secrets, cert-manager, Traefik, Prometheus operator, and Grafana operator (plus Metrics Server on cloud). Wait gates: cnpg-controller-manager, cert-manager-webhook, external-secrets-operator, external-secrets-operator-webhook.
  2. infra-phase2, trust distribution. trust-manager, plus the cluster issuers on cloud. Wait gate: trust-manager.
  3. monitoring, observability. Grafana, Loki, Alloy, and Prometheus into the monitoring namespace.
  4. opendefense, applications. CFSSL → PKI → opendefense-system (Keycloak, LDAP, RM API, RM UI, miniwerk) → Battlelog → TAK → MediaMTX.

The ordering matters. The applications can't start without the CA from opendefense-cfssl, the trust roots from trust-manager, and the operators from infra-phase1 already in place. Skip a phase and you'll usually get a pod flapping on some cryptic certificate or CRD error.

Two environments

local cloud
Target kind cluster on the workstation k3s VM (k3s-azure.yaml)
Composition entry point k8s/main/local/ k8s/main/cloud/
Hostname localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi (loopback) Set at deploy time via OPENDEFENSE_HOST (Zarf var)
Lifecycle command task up / task deploy task zarf:package:cloud → zarf package deploy
Storage hostPath via kind k3s default storage class
TLS issuer Self-signed via in-cluster CFSSL Same, plus cloud-specific ClusterIssuers

The cloud composition does two things the local one skips:

  • It strips Helm ownership metadata so Zarf can adopt resources without fighting Helm.
  • It splits infra-phase1 into one Zarf manifest per bundle (cert-manager, cloudnative-pg, external-secrets-operator, grafana-operator, keycloak-operator, traefik). That keeps the rendered Helm output under Kubernetes' Secret size limit.

Hostnames and routing

Every integrated product publishes two hostnames:

  • <product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST>, public, TLS-only.
  • mtls.<product>.<OPENDEFENSE_HOST>, the mutual-TLS variant for clients authenticating with a client certificate (TAK, internal admin tools, and so on).

Traefik fronts both. TAK also needs raw TCP passthrough on 8089 (CoT streaming) and 8443 (TAK native HTTPS). MediaMTX needs ports 1936, 8322, 8890, 9888, and 9889 for its streaming protocols. The local kind-config.yaml pre-maps all of these to the host.

When something is wrong

  • A pod dropping into CrashLoopBackOff early in the boot usually means an infra-phase1 controller isn't ready yet and its CRDs are missing. Re-run task deploy and let the wait gates catch up.
  • TLS errors between services usually mean trust-manager never distributed the CFSSL CA bundle into the namespace that's complaining. Check there.
  • A new service that never shows up in the RM UI is almost always missing from MW_PRODUCTS. Check that first.
  • When a Zarf deploy fails on Secret size, a Helm-rendered manifest has gone over the limit. Give it a fresh bundle subfolder under k8s/main/cloud/infra-phase1/bundles/ instead of cramming more into one that already exists.
